### BR-0161: P2 - Contain archive preflight failures within each batch item

- [ ] OPEN
- Type: defect
- Confidence: high
- Category: correctness/resource-lifetime
- Found by: R1-CHUNK-0065, R1-CHUNK-0091
- Location: `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:android/helpers/run_mission_zip_batch.ps1:L657-L716` before the per-archive `try`
- Related: `android/helpers/run_mission_zip_batch.ps1:L406-L477,L745-L792` and `android/ai tool plans/testing/plan_mission_zip_batch_manual_run_20260609.md:L3-L16`
- Evidence: The batch's stated design is to record each ZIP failure, continue, and report all failures. Instead, it hashes the complete file and inspects its archive contents before entering the per-item `try`. `ZipFile.OpenRead` and entry enumeration for ZIP files are not caught, so one corrupt, truncated, unreadable, or concurrently removed ZIP terminates the entire script before that archive has a record and before later archives or the final summaries run. The 500 MiB skip check occurs only after this hashing and parsing, so the configured limit does not protect preflight work. The 7z branch handles the same inspection failure differently: it converts the error to an `unknown` hint, which the loop records as a skip rather than a failure.
- Trigger: Place a corrupt ZIP between two valid archives, make a selected file unreadable or remove it after enumeration, select an oversized ZIP intended to be skipped, or make 7-Zip listing fail for a selected `.7z`
- Impact: ZIP failures abort the batch and omit later results and final summaries; oversized files still consume full hashing and archive-inspection work before being skipped; and equivalent 7z failures can be reported as harmless skips, allowing inconsistent and incomplete regeneration evidence
- Expected: The size gate runs before expensive inspection, every fallible operation after enumeration belongs to one initialized item record, inspection failures are failed items, and recoverable per-item failures cannot prevent later records or final summary publication
- Suggested fix: Initialize a minimal record first, apply the size policy before hashing or opening the archive, and move hashing, classification, template resolution, device work, and recoverable artifact capture under one per-item exception boundary. Represent inspection success separately from `unknown` game classification, mark tool or parser errors failed, and funnel all item completion through one record-and-continue path. Reserve whole-batch termination for failures that make further processing or truthful output impossible.
- Validation: Run ordered good-corrupt-good ZIPs, a bad 7z file, an unreadable or disappearing file, an oversized sparse file, a nested-archive error, device failure, and local artifact-write failure. Assert exact per-item statuses, no pre-limit archive parsing, continued execution where possible, one record per selected input, complete final summaries, and nonzero exit whenever any selected input failed.

- Suggested fix: Call `Cleanup` unconditionally from `finally`; extend it to stop, wait for, and dispose both logcat processes and the relay, close redirected streams, and remove emulator redirections where appropriate. - Expected: The helper binds loopback by default, accepts host replies only from the configured redirection endpoint, rejects unknown sources, and establishes or changes the joiner endpoint through a deliberate test-controlled rule
- Suggested fix: Default and normally restrict binding to loopback, compare host traffic against the exact configured redirection endpoint, and drop unknown endpoints with rate-limited diagnostics. Establish the joiner through an explicit expected address, one-time random test nonce, or controlled startup handshake; if rebinding is required, make it an explicit authenticated or parent-commanded transition rather than any-source learning.
- Validation: Use separate legitimate host, legitimate joiner, pre-learning spoof, and post-learning third-party sockets on loopback and a reachable non-loopback interface. Assert only the two intended endpoints receive data, spoofing cannot claim or replace either role, zero-length and malformed packets are handled safely, legitimate bidirectional traffic remains intact, and the default listener is unreachable off-host.

- Related: `game_data/extract_dos_demos.ps1:L115-L270` and BR-0020
- Evidence: Each package uses the predictable shared tree `%TEMP%\dxx_dosbox_<sanitized-name>` and recursively deletes it before starting, so concurrent invocations for the same package can erase or modify each other's mounted files. The package body has no `try/finally`; exceptions or interruption after `Start-Process` can bypass both process termination and directory cleanup. The normal kill path neither waits for confirmed exit nor disposes the process object or terminates an owned child tree, and final cleanup suppresses every error, allowing a live DOSBox process, locks, or stale staging data to survive.

- Impact: Runs can delete or publish each other's data, orphan emulator processes, retain proprietary expanded installer contents, and make later retries fail or consume stale bytes nondeterministically
- Expected: Every invocation has collision-free temporary ownership and a guaranteed cleanup path that stops only its process tree, waits for termination, disposes handles, and reports retained resources without destroying another run's state
- Suggested fix: Create a cryptographically unique private temp directory per invocation, preflight or lock final output ownership, and wrap each package in `try/finally`. Retain the exact process handle or a Windows job object, terminate only that owned tree on timeout or failure, wait and dispose it, then perform checked cleanup while preserving diagnostics and a prior complete output generation.
- Validation: Run barrier-synchronized invocations of the same and different packages, inject exceptions and interruption after every lifecycle phase, spawn an owned child, hold staging files open, and force kill and cleanup failures; assert no cross-run deletion or publication, no owned process survives, residue is identified and recoverable, and valid sequential runs remain deterministic.
- Additional location (R1-CHUNK-0069): `game_data/extract_mac_cd.ps1:L104-L110,L165-L205,L269-L332,L369-L380,L439-L445` in temporary-tree, stream, and child-process ownership

File streams use explicit close calls rather than guaranteed disposal and child processes have no owned cancellation path; exceptions or interruption can leave handles or descendants that make the final recursive cleanup mask the original failure or retain proprietary staging data.
- Additional validation (R1-CHUNK-0069): Run barrier-synchronized invocations for the same CD, inject exceptions after every open and child launch, stall each child, hold staged files open, and force cleanup failure; assert unique temporary ownership, no cross-run deletion, deterministic child-tree termination, preserved primary diagnostics, and identified recoverable residue.
- Additional location (R1-CHUNK-0070): `game_data/extract_mac_demos.ps1:L126-L145,L198` in per-package temporary-tree ownership and cleanup
- Additional evidence (R1-CHUNK-0070): Each Mac package uses the predictable shared tree `%TEMP%\dxx_mac_demo_<sanitized-basename>` and recursively deletes it before extraction. Concurrent invocations of the same package can therefore erase or replace each other's source and nested trees. There is no per-package `try/finally`; an unar, copy, hash, or interruption failure exits before cleanup, while normal cleanup suppresses every error and cannot establish that the synchronous extractor or temporary proprietary contents are gone.

- [ ] OPEN
- Type: defect

- Category: compatibility/correctness

- Location: `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:android/app/src/main/cpp/extract/cue_parser.c:L96-L108,L135-L159` in track-mode parsing and sector-count calculation
- Related: `android/app/src/main/cpp/extract/cue_parser.h:L22-L26,L35-L41`, `android/app/src/main/cpp/extract/iso9660_reader.c:L55-L57,L106-L116`, `android/app/src/main/cpp/extract/extract_cd.c:L448-L537`, `android/app/src/main/cpp/extract/test_cue_iso.c:L1256-L1275`, [ECMA-130](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-130/), and [ECMA-168](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-168_2nd_edition_december_1994.pdf)
- Evidence: The parser classifies every TRACK token other than an AUDIO prefix as the same data type, discards the mode string, and divides every final data-file byte length by the hard-coded 2,352-byte sector size. Extraction then sends every data track through a reader whose geometry is fixed to 2,352-byte sectors with a 16-byte Mode 1 payload offset. The assigned `MODE2/2352` test calls that input valid but asserts only the generic data classification. ECMA-130 defines a Mode 2 Form 1 sector with an additional eight-byte subheader before its 2,048-byte data field, so its payload begins at byte 24 rather than byte 16; 2,048-byte data-track images likewise require a 2,048-byte stride and no raw-sector header. Unknown TRACK modes are also silently accepted as data.
- Trigger: Import a BIN/CUE whose data track is declared `MODE2/2352` and contains an XA Form 1 ISO, use a supported 2,048-byte data-track representation, or supply an unknown TRACK mode
- Impact: A declared-valid Mode 2 image is read eight bytes before each logical payload, so primary-volume recognition, directory listing, and extraction fail or consume incorrect data. Other modes receive wrong sector counts, offsets, and hashes, while unknown formats can be misinterpreted instead of rejected.
- Expected: Parsing preserves the exact supported data-track format, each downstream reader and hasher uses that format's sector stride and payload geometry, and unsupported or unknown modes fail before metadata, hashes, or files are published.
- Suggested fix: Replace the generic data classification with explicit supported sector formats, retain AUDIO separately, compute source sectors with the selected stride, and pass checked sector geometry into hashing and ISO readers. Reject ambiguous, unsupported, and unknown mode tokens; if Mode 2 Form 2 is intentionally unsupported, report that limitation explicitly rather than treating it as an ISO data track.
- Validation: Add exact listing, extraction, and hashing cases for Mode 1/2352, Mode 1/2048, and Mode 2/2352 XA Form 1; add Mode 2 Form 2, unknown-token, mixed-track, and multi-file rejection or support cases; and verify each accepted format uses the expected stride, payload offset, sector count, digest bytes, and extracted content.

- Evidence: Every extraction-test exit reads the complete checked-in spec, replaces `last_test_result`, and calls `File.WriteAllText` on the canonical pathname. Generation uses the same writer. `WriteAllText` opens the destination for replacement, truncating the prior valid file before the complete new JSON is durable; there is no same-directory temporary file, flush and close gate, atomic replace, backup, or per-path writer lock. Process termination, storage exhaustion, or an I/O failure can therefore leave the only regression oracle empty or partial. Two same-spec runners can also read the same old generation and let the later final-path write silently discard the first result. Readiness checks only that the pathname is a leaf, so a truncated file can still be reported ready and will not trigger oracle recovery before later parsing fails.
- Trigger: Stop or crash a test while it persists its result, exhaust or fail storage during a spec write, interrupt forced generation, or run two tests or generators against the same spec concurrently
- Impact: Routine validation can corrupt a tracked regression input, lose a newer result, or leave generation partially updated; subsequent validation and extraction runs then fail to parse or consume stale policy while automatic readiness incorrectly treats the damaged pathname as complete
- Expected: Readers observe either the complete prior spec or the complete validated replacement, and concurrent writers cannot lose updates silently
- Suggested fix: Serialize updates by normalized spec path, reread and merge inside the transaction, write UTF-8 to a unique same-directory temporary file, flush and close it, parse or otherwise validate the completed bytes, then atomically replace the destination while retaining the prior valid generation on failure. Prefer storing mutable run results outside tracked oracle inputs so ordinary tests do not rewrite their own source of truth.
- Validation: Inject open, partial-write, flush, close, validation, replace, process-interruption, and disk-full failures with an existing valid spec; race distinct result updates and generation against result persistence. Assert the old file survives every failed publication, successful files parse and contain the intended generation, readiness rejects damaged files, and concurrent behavior follows a documented no-lost-update policy.

### BR-0195: P1 - Authenticate cooperative state-packet authority

- [ ] OPEN
- Type: defect
- Confidence: high
- Category: security/protocol-integrity
- Found by: R1-CHUNK-0101, R1-CHUNK-0119, R1-CHUNK-0122, R1-CHUNK-0141, R1-CHUNK-0204
- Location: `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/coop/coop_multi_status.c:L75-L82,L159-L192`; `android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/coop/coop_warp.c:L333-L365`; `android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/multi_save_transfer.c:L79-L84,L770-L805`; `d1/main/multi.c:L3323-L3346,L5707-L5708`; and `d2/main/multi.c:L3486-L3509,L7620-L7621` in cooperative packet application
- Related: `android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/android_rewind_policy.c:L39-L47`, `android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/difficulty_runtime_shared.c:L76-L117`, `d1/main/multi.c:L5567-L5708`, `d2/main/multi.c:L7355-L7621`, `d1/main/net_udp.c:L6721-L6804`, `d2/main/net_udp.c:L6881-L6958`, and BR-0080
- Evidence: The new handlers trust identity or authority encoded inside the multiplayer payload. `coop_do_peer_status` writes the claimed slot's kill statistics without comparing it with the authenticated outer UDP sender. More seriously, `coop_do_restore_inventory` checks only that the claimed target equals the local player, then applies attacker-controlled energy, shields, score, laser level, weapon flags, twenty ammo values, durable flags, lifetime statistics, and time totals. `coop_warp_do_packet` similarly accepts a payload-selected warper slot, valid segment, and coordinates, then moves and relinks that claimed player's object without requiring the claimed warper to match the authenticated sender. The paired `multi_do_difficulty` handlers likewise authorize solely by comparing the payload's claimed sender byte with `multi_who_is_master`; a non-host can copy the public master slot into byte 1 and choose any admitted difficulty. The handler then changes live AI, weapon, damage, scoring, history, `Netgame`, HUD, and player-default state and writes the receiving player's profile. Rewind requests add the same identity flaw: `multi_do_rewind_request` treats payload byte 1 as the requester, checks only that some connected or waiting player occupies that slot, indexes its one-second throttle by the claimed slot, and sends results to that slot. On the host, the UDP layer authenticates a peer only against the outer `pnum`, then forwards the complete inner message to every other player before local dispatch. D2 carries that authenticated slot into `multi_process_data_from_player` but passes it only to a later escort-owner handler, not to these cooperative handlers; D1 discards it before dispatch. A non-host peer can therefore send a valid restore packet with another player's slot in byte 1, a warp packet claiming another connected player and arbitrary accepted destination coordinates, a difficulty packet claiming the master, or rewind requests that cycle through other connected slots. The host accepts and relays the state packets; recipients apply the trusted-host copy to live state, while forged rewind identities bypass the intended per-client throttle and misdirect results. The same path lets a peer attribute arbitrary status totals to another slot. BR-0080 covers unsafe ship-status indices and their memory-safety impact; this finding covers the distinct identity, authority, and cooperative state-integrity failure in the new message types.
- Trigger: Join an Android cooperative D1 or D2 game with a modified peer; send `MULTI_COOP_RESTORE_INV` through the normal multiplayer channel with the victim's player number and chosen record fields, send `MULTI_COOP_PEER_STATUS` with another connected player's number, send `MULTI_WARP_TO_PLAYER` with the victim as the claimed warper and chosen valid segment and coordinates, send `MULTI_DIFFICULTY` with the master slot in byte 1 and an attacker-selected value in byte 2, or enable client rewind requests and rapidly send `MULTI_REWIND_REQUEST` while cycling byte 1 through connected player slots
- Impact: Any admitted participant can remotely replace another player's combat inventory, score, progression totals, and selected durable state, falsify another player's cooperative statistics, teleport and relink another player's object, force the global difficulty and persist that forced choice as each recipient's default, or bypass the rewind requester's per-second throttle in proportion to the number of occupied slots while attributing requests and responses to victims. Validate the locked buffer's reported format before writing and fail clearly or convert when it differs.

Generate a unique replay-owned name in a dedicated temporary namespace, create it without replacing an existing path, track ownership explicitly, and remove only that owned file after close and restore. ### BR-0227: P2 - Preserve cooperative warp targets through cycle and send

- [ ] OPEN
- Type: defect
- Confidence: high
- Category: gameplay/state-integrity
- Found by: R1-CHUNK-0119
- Location: `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/coop/coop_warp.c:L158-L171,L230-L238,L241-L283,L305-L326` in target selection and packet construction
- Related: `android/app/src/main/java/com/dxxredux/app/WarpButtonOverlay.kt:L73-L94,L130-L168` and `android/app/src/main/cpp/jni_main.c:L1193-L1255`
- Evidence: `coop_find_next_target` performs only `N_players` probes but wraps each candidate with `% MAX_PLAYERS`. Player slots are contiguous below `N_players`, so after `coop_warp_cycle_target` increments beyond the highest occupied slot the scan can spend every probe on unused slots instead of wrapping through the occupied range. With two players, cycling from valid target 1 starts at 2 and checks only 2 and 3, missing target 1. The Kotlin poll then receives unavailable status and hides the only warp control, so the player cannot cycle again to recover. Successful sends lose the chosen target by a second route: `coop_warp_execute` records cooldown before calling `coop_warp_send_packet`, and the sender calls `coop_warp_get_status` again to obtain the target byte. The cooldown early return leaves the zero-initialized status target at slot 0, so every successful packet reports target 0 even when placement used another player; remote HUD text consequently names the wrong destination player.
- Trigger: In a two-player cooperative game with the teammate eligible, long-press the warp control once; or in any cooperative game successfully warp to an eligible player whose slot is not zero
- Impact: Cycling can make the warp control disappear and leave warp unavailable until unrelated state resets it, while successful nonzero-target warps serialize misleading target identity to every peer. Players lose the advertised target-selection control and observers receive incorrect event attribution.
- Expected: Cycling examines every occupied player slot exactly once and wraps to an eligible target, and the packet for a successful warp carries the exact target used to calculate and apply that warp.
- Suggested fix: Iterate occupied slots with modulo `N_players` after handling the zero-player case, publish the cursor only after a valid target is selected, and pass the already validated `status.target_pnum` explicitly from execute into packet construction instead of re-querying status after cooldown changes.
- Validation: Add paired D1 and D2 tests for two through `MAX_PLAYERS` slots with local, disconnected, dead, nearby, and eligible combinations; cycle past the highest slot and require wraparound without hiding the control when an eligible target exists. Execute against each nonzero target and assert the serialized target byte, placement reference, sender log, and every receiver HUD message all identify the same player.

- Evidence: The public policy structure contains one pointer, one `int`, and three callback pointers but establishes no local packing boundary. The shared implementation includes this header first and therefore compiles it under MSVC's default pack-8 state. Both engine adapters include `args.h` and other engine headers first; their transitive `pstypes.h` executes `#pragma pack(push, packing)` followed by `#pragma pack(1)` without restoring that state before the policy header, so each adapter defines the same named structure under pack 1. On Win64, the engine object is 36 bytes with callback offsets 12, 20, and 28, while the shared implementation reads a 40-byte layout with callback offsets 16, 24, and 32. The first callback read therefore combines halves of adjacent engine pointers, and the last reads four bytes beyond the object. The standalone test includes the policy header before any engine header, so it constructs the same default layout as the shared implementation and cannot detect the production include-order mismatch.
- Trigger: Build D1 or D2 for MSVC x64 and play a replay frame containing death-abort, difficulty-change, or game-specific direct commands through the paired engine adapter
- Impact: The shared dispatcher can indirect-call a fabricated callback address or read beyond the policy object, causing an immediate access violation or unpredictable native control flow. Command-bearing deterministic replay is therefore unusable and memory-unsafe in an officially packaged Windows configuration.
- Expected: The policy has one explicit ABI with identical size and field offsets in shared C, paired engine C, tests, and every supported compiler, independent of ambient packing and include order.
- Suggested fix: Give this cross-translation-unit structure a locally balanced explicit layout boundary, such as MSVC `#pragma pack(push, 8)` and matching pop, with equivalent compiler guarantees where required, or hide the representation behind constructor and accessor functions so callers never instantiate it. Do not depend on packing inherited from unrelated engine headers.
- Validation: Add C compile-time assertions for `sizeof` and every `offsetof` in the shared implementation and in paired D1 and D2 translation units after `pstypes.h`, plus header tests under default, pack-1, and pack-16 outer states that confirm the caller's state is preserved. - Expected: Any direct-command retrieval, validation, or application failure terminates the replay with a preserved failure reason before game simulation or frame advancement.
- Suggested fix: Return a typed controls outcome that distinguishes ordinary simulation, command-consumed frame, and terminal failure, and make the shared step stop on the latter. As a minimal containment, unload or explicitly mark D1 failed before returning, but preserve an error state that headless and interactive completion cannot reinterpret as normal end-of-replay.

Concurrent writers use separate locks around `lseek(SEEK_END)` followed by ordinary `write`, without `O_APPEND` or an interprocess lock, so records can overwrite or interleave; any later installer can also erase another live process's snapshot. A report can therefore implicate the wrong subsystem and lose the actual sequence, undermining the isolation that the branch explicitly introduced to contain native crashes.
- Expected: Each process lifetime owns a distinct snapshot that cannot be removed or written by another process, and backfill attaches only the snapshot produced by the exact crashed process lifetime.
- Suggested fix: Include a stable process name plus PID and process-start token in the snapshot name, make native initialization idempotent for that lifetime, and pass or derive the same identity in the xCrash callback and backfill path. Use create-new or atomic replacement for owned snapshots, and prune only stale snapshots whose owners are gone. Do not select an artifact solely by a broad timestamp window.
- Validation: Run the launcher, game, both preview processes, and both metadata workers concurrently with distinct breadcrumb prefixes and repeated Activity or service recreation. Crash each process in turn and assert its tombstone receives only that process lifetime's complete ordered records, no live snapshot is unlinked by another installer, simultaneous writes do not overlap, and stale owned snapshots are eventually pruned without touching active ones.

Their merged-wall renderer binds the bottom texture on unit 0, switches to unit 1 for the overlay and sometimes unit 2 for a mask, then returns to unit 0 without invalidating or partitioning the cache. After a non-super draw with bottom A and overlay B, unit 0 still contains A, unit 1 contains B, and the scalar contains B. If the next wall uses B as its bottom, the unit-0 bind is skipped even though unit 0 does not contain B; the shader samples stale A. The cached GPU texmerge path also calls the assigned helper on units 0 and 1 through the same scalar, so equal or repeated handles can produce the same false reuse there. Per-frame reset does not repair incorrect binds within the frame, and the reuse counter reports the skipped operation as an optimization.

This produces scene-order-dependent wrong or flickering geometry in both games and can hide or replace gameplay-relevant wall and door visuals while diagnostics falsely report a successful cached bind reuse.
- Expected: A bind is skipped only when the requested target is already bound on the currently active texture unit; transitions among units cannot borrow another unit's cache entry.
- Suggested fix: Replace the scalar with binding state indexed by texture unit, and route every engine and shared-helper bind plus each raw bind or deletion through one cache-aware API. Either pass the intended unit explicitly or query and validate `GL_ACTIVE_TEXTURE` at state-transition boundaries; invalidate all affected entries after bulk filter updates, texture deletion, context recreation, and external diagnostic binds. If the small optimization cannot be made complete, issue `glBindTexture` unconditionally in multitexture paths.
- Validation: Add a GLES state test with distinct sentinel textures A, B, and C. Bind A on unit 0 and B on unit 1, return to unit 0, request B, and assert `GL_TEXTURE_BINDING_2D` becomes B rather than remaining A; repeat across unit 2, equal bottom/overlay handles, deletion, recreation, direct diagnostic binds, and cached texmerge. ### BR-0271: P2 - Measure texture-burst gaps from load boundaries

- [ ] OPEN
- Type: defect
- Confidence: high
- Category: correctness/observability
- Found by: R1-CHUNK-0157
- Location: `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/android_profile.c:L221-L225,L266-L307` in texture-burst timing and idle admission
- Related: `android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/android_profile.c:L578-L663`, paired `d1/arch/ogl/ogl.c:L3280,L3379,L3567`, paired `d2/arch/ogl/ogl.c:L3358,L3481,L3676`, `android/helpers/summarize-profiling-log.ps1:L223-L244,L322-L348`, and `android/ai tool plans/crash, logging, diagnostics/plan_profiling_log_category_20260521.md:L31-L51,L284-L301`
- Evidence: Texture profiling is called after a load completes and receives that load's elapsed `total_us`, but burst admission samples only the current completion time. It first compares that completion against the previous completion to decide whether at least 250 ms of idle occurred, then starts a new burst at the same completion timestamp. Two back-to-back loads therefore split whenever the second load itself lasts at least 250 ms even though their actual idle gap is zero. A single-load burst always has `start_us == last_end_us` and reports `span_us=0` regardless of whether the load took milliseconds or seconds. The branch added burst summaries specifically to group level-start and reload storms after an earlier capture underreported them, so this boundary error defeats the intended diagnostic case.
- Trigger: Profile one texture load of any positive duration, or profile two immediately consecutive loads where the later load takes at least 250 ms
- Impact: Burst span is understated by the complete first-load duration, isolated slow loads report a zero span, and uninterrupted storms containing a sufficiently slow load fragment into separate bursts labeled as idle-separated. Counts, averages, rankings, and correlation with the long frame then misrepresent the texture storm the profiler was introduced to diagnose.
- Expected: Burst span covers the first admitted load through the last load completion, and the idle threshold measures only the gap from the previous load's end to the next load's start.
- Suggested fix: Capture or pass both start and end monotonic timestamps for every load. Compare `current_start_us - previous_end_us` for idle admission, initialize `start_us` from the first load start, and retain `last_end_us` from its completion. If only elapsed duration is available, derive a checked approximate start as `end_us - max(total_us, 0)` and document that contract.
- Validation: Add a deterministic clock test for one load, back-to-back short and 250 ms or longer loads, gaps just below, at, and above 250 ms, mixed slow and fast storms, sample-boundary and explicit flush reasons, and invalid negative durations. Assert exact burst counts, load counts, spans, totals, maxima, reasons, and parser ranking.
- Resolution: Pending

- Location: `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/cd_preview.c:L245-L249,L292-L308,L336-L357` in producer EOF and callback consumption

- Evidence: The render thread sets `s_playing` to zero as soon as it reaches source EOF, writes any final generated chunk into the ring, and exits. The OpenSL callback reads the ring only while `s_playing` is nonzero, so after that store it outputs silence and never consumes the final chunk or any older queued PCM. The ring holds 262,144 samples, or about 2.73 seconds of stereo audio at the normal 48 kHz output rate, and the producer deliberately fills it ahead of playback. The state poll observes stopped immediately and forces the displayed position to the full duration, masking the missing tail. Because the callback unconditionally re-enqueues its silent buffer, the OpenSL player also keeps waking and outputting silence until an explicit stop or dialog disposal.

- Impact: Ordinary launcher previews lose up to roughly the ring's buffered duration from their ending, while the UI falsely shows complete playback and the MIDI position can run the same buffer depth ahead before completion. The native audio queue then remains active and repeatedly schedules silent callbacks for as long as the completed dialog stays open.
- Expected: Producer EOF is distinct from playback completion; callbacks drain every generated frame, completion becomes visible only after the last queued frame is consumed, and the native player then reaches a terminal quiescent state.
- Suggested fix: Track producer-done separately from playing, let the callback drain the ring after producer EOF, and publish stopped only when queued PCM and the final OpenSL buffer are complete. Hand terminal teardown to a safe non-callback owner so the callback chain stops without destroying itself.
- Validation: Use tracks shorter than one ring, exactly one ring, and several rings with sentinel samples in the final seconds at 44.1 and 48 kHz output. Assert every expected final sample is delivered once, position advances rather than jumping, stopped appears only after drain, no callbacks continue after terminal cleanup, and explicit stop still truncates promptly by design.
- Additional location (R1-CHUNK-0202): `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/midi_preview.c:L87-L91,L287-L379,L403-L417,L683-L694` in MIDI production, callback consumption, and state publication
- Additional evidence (R1-CHUNK-0202): The MIDI preview repeats the same ring and terminal-state defect. Its producer advances `s_playback_msec` while filling as much as 262,144 interleaved samples ahead of the OpenSL consumer, and `get_state` reports that generated clock rather than consumed audio time. At the last MIDI message, rendering sets `s_playing=0`, writes any final chunk, and exits; the callback reads the ring only when `s_playing` remains true, so it immediately switches to silence and strands the final chunk plus older buffered samples. The UI can therefore run about 2.73 seconds ahead at 48 kHz stereo and then display full duration and stopped while the corresponding ending was never heard, while the callback continues re-enqueueing silence.
- Additional validation (R1-CHUNK-0202): Apply the sentinel-output matrix to MIDI and HMP tracks and sample the reported position against callback-consumed frames throughout playback, not only at EOF. - Suggested fix: Extract a shared clipping helper that solves the segment-sphere quadratic with widened fixed-point intermediates, clamps roots to the segment interval, and emits the one or two outside subsegments. Use one documented distance metric consistently for classification and intersection, and retain the anchored first-segment fast path only as an optional optimization.
- Validation: Unit-test centered radial egress, oblique inside-to-outside and outside-to-inside chords, outside-to-outside miss, tangent, and two-intersection crossing cases in both directions, plus zero-length and boundary endpoints. ### BR-0303: P1 - Free cached merged-wall textures before clearing their owners

- [ ] OPEN
- Type: defect
- Confidence: high
- Category: resource-lifetime/graphics
- Found by: R1-CHUNK-0191
- Location: `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/merged_wall_debug.c:L483-L507,L568-L581` in cached texmerge clearing and reset
- Related: `android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/merged_wall_debug.c:L922-L960`, `d1/arch/ogl/ogl.c:L409-L501,L636-L705,L3590-L3608`, `d2/arch/ogl/ogl.c:L397-L510,L647-L716,L3698-L3716`, `d1/main/game.c:L756-L765`, `d2/main/game.c:L898-L907`, `d1/main/gameseq.c:L721-L741`, `d2/main/gameseq.c:L1853-L1858,L928-L938`, and `d1/include/internal.h:L9`
- Evidence: Each completed cache entry owns a standalone texture obtained from the global `ogl_texture_list`; eviction and setup failure pass that pointer to `ogl_freetexture`, which deletes its GL handle, decrements the texture count, and resets the list slot. In contrast, `android_merged_wall_cached_texmerge_clear_cache` calls the generic clear loop, and that loop only resets each entry. Reset immediately assigns `entry->texture = NULL`, permanently discarding the only cache ownership pointer without deleting the GL object or resetting its list slot. The palette-invalidation path invokes this clear and then frees only parent `GameBitmaps`, which cannot reach the standalone merged outputs. Both level loading and ordinary `palette_restore` invoke palette invalidation during a live context, while multiplayer adds another clear after paging. A populated clear can therefore strand all 32 cache textures; repeated restores or level transitions accumulate GL memory and occupied entries in the fixed 20,000-slot texture list until a later whole-list smash happens to delete the handles.
- Trigger: Populate the Android plain merged-wall cache by rendering at least one overlaid wall, then restore the saved palette or load another level without destroying the GL context; repeat after repopulating the cache
- Impact: GPU texture memory and global texture-list capacity grow across ordinary in-process palette and level transitions. On long sessions or high-resolution texture packs this can cause GL allocation failures or driver out-of-memory behavior, and continued slot loss eventually terminates through `Error("OGL: texture list full!")`.
- Expected: Every cache invalidation releases each owned output texture exactly once before forgetting the pointer, while whole-context teardown remains free of double deletion.
- Suggested fix: Give the cache-clear lifecycle an explicit texture-free callback or paired OGL-owned wrapper, call `ogl_freetexture` for every non-null cached texture before resetting the entry, and define teardown ordering so the cache releases or relinquishes ownership before bulk texture-list reset/delete. Keep the generic entry-reset helper non-owning and use it only after ownership has been discharged.
- Validation: Add a focused cache-lifetime test with a counting free callback for empty, partial, and full 32-entry caches, including repeated clears and reinitialization. On both D1 and D2 Android builds, instrument GL deletes, `r_texcount`, and occupied texture-list slots while repeatedly populating then invoking palette restore, level palette invalidation, multiplayer post-load clear, PNG smash, and full context smash; require no monotonic growth, one delete per owned texture, no double delete, and successful cache reuse afterward with stock and high-resolution textures.
- Resolution: Pending

### BR-0304: P2 - Bind each merged-wall source before changing its wrap state

- [ ] OPEN
- Type: defect
- Confidence: high
- Category: correctness/graphics
- Found by: R1-CHUNK-0192
- Location: `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/merged_wall_debug.c:L761-L889` in cached merged-wall FBO composition
- Related: `android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/merged_wall_debug.c:L582-L591`, `d1/arch/ogl/ogl.c:L619-L628,L1405-L1452`, `d2/arch/ogl/ogl.c:L630-L639,L1414-L1461`, `android/ai tool plans/overlay, menu, etc/overlay-rendering-four-cases.md:L18-L26`, and `android/game_scripts/test_merged_wall_snapshot_regression.json5:L53-L82`
- Evidence: The shared wrap helper has the same contract as paired `ogl_texwrap`: it issues `glTexParameteri` against the currently bound texture and does not bind the object passed to it. The paired cached-merge caller enters with texture unit zero active, bottom bound on unit zero, overlay bound on unit one, and both source wrap states set to `GL_REPEAT`. The compositor then calls the helper for bottom and overlay consecutively before its first `glActiveTexture`; both GL calls therefore affect the bottom texture on unit zero. Nevertheless the second call writes `overlay_bmp->gltexture->wrapstate = GL_CLAMP_TO_EDGE`, so metadata claims the overlay changed while its real unit-one state remains `GL_REPEAT` throughout the offscreen draw. The later restore repeats the same object-versus-binding mistake before marking both metadata objects as repeat. This matters in the explicitly supported partial-pack cases where one wall source is 64x64 and the other is high resolution: the output uses the larger dimension, so with bilinear or trilinear filtering, samples of the smaller source at the first and last output pixels do not land on its edge texel centers. Repeat blends across opposite edges while the requested clamp would retain the nearest edge, changing cached color and alpha at the composite boundary. The maintained route test checks only metadata and route selection, not wrap state or rendered pixels.
- Trigger: Enable bilinear or trilinear world filtering and render a plain transparent merged wall whose bottom and overlay GL textures have different visible dimensions, such as a partial high-resolution texture pack replacing only one member of the pair
- Impact: The cached composite can contain color or transparency bleeding from the opposite edge of the smaller source. That incorrect border is mipmapped, cached, and reused for every wall with the same texture pair and orientation, producing seams or wrong edge pixels in both D1 and D2.
- Expected: Each source has the intended wrap parameters applied to its own GL object before FBO sampling, and its cached `wrapstate` always describes the actual object state.
- Suggested fix: Select and bind bottom on unit zero before changing bottom wrap, then select and bind overlay on unit one before changing overlay wrap; restore each object while its own unit is active. Integrate this ordering with the per-unit binding-state fix from BR-0256, or use a helper that accepts the intended unit and performs a cache-aware bind before `glTexParameteri`.
- Validation: Add a GLES test using bottom and overlay sentinel textures with distinct first and last edge colors at 64x64 versus 512x512. Under nearest, bilinear, and trilinear settings and all four orientations, query both source objects' wrap parameters, render the cached composite, and compare its border pixels against an independently clamped reference. Repeat with stock/stock, high-resolution/high-resolution, high-resolution/stock, stock/high-resolution, NPOT visible extents, cache reuse, and failure cleanup in paired D1 and D2; require metadata and live GL state to agree and no opposite-edge bleed.
- Resolution: Pending

- Suggested fix: Keep tracking and geometric comparisons canvas-local by using `canvas_w/2, canvas_h/2`, then add `bm_x/bm_y` exactly once when converting a selected sample to full-frame framebuffer coordinates. - [ ] OPEN

- Confidence: high
- Category: correctness/diagnostics

- Location: `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/merged_wall_debug.c:L3496-L3658` in texture GPU readback comparison
- Related: `d1/arch/ogl/ogl.c:L3039-L3074,L3085-L3299,L3300-L3394`, `d2/arch/ogl/ogl.c:L3115-L3389,L3390-L3496`, `d1/2d/bitmap.c:L31-L41`, `d2/2d/bitmap.c:L31-L41`, and `android/ai tool plans/crash, logging, diagnostics/coop_texture_ten_round_logging_20260707.md:L15-L20`
- Evidence: The readback helper obtains the original indexed game bitmap through `merged_wall_get_source_bitmap` and enables a pixel-for-pixel expected-RGBA comparison whenever that bitmap's dimensions equal the GL texture dimensions. It never excludes `texture->is_png`. Both paired replacement loaders upload PNG data or KTX2 storage into the GL texture, mark that texture `is_png = 1`, preserve the original `bm_data`, and release the temporary replacement buffer. A supported replacement whose dimensions happen to equal the stock bitmap therefore enters `compare=1`, but every intentionally changed replacement pixel is compared against palette-expanded stock content. The resulting `[mwall_texread]` record reports nonzero `mismatches`, an unrelated stock `expected_rgba` hash, and stock expected samples even though the GPU upload can exactly match the selected replacement.
- Trigger: Install a PNG or KTX2 replacement for a logged base or overlay wall texture with the same width and height as its stock game bitmap, then request the maintained merged-wall snapshot, crosshair probe, tap probe, or all-face readback
- Impact: Correct replacement uploads are diagnosed as corrupted or palette-mismatched textures, while a stock pixel that happens to match provides accidental partial success. Investigators using the readback specifically to distinguish source, upload, palette, and merge failures can pursue the wrong layer, and automated or manual conclusions based on `mismatches=0` are not valid across supported replacement packs.
- Expected: Expected-pixel comparison uses the exact byte source and conversion semantics uploaded to the current GL object, or explicitly reports comparison unavailable when that source is no longer retained; stock bitmap pixels are never presented as the expected content of a replacement-backed texture.
- Suggested fix: Carry a source identity and retained or reproducible expected hash/pixels through each stock, PNG, and KTX2 upload generation. Let readback compare only when that identity and conversion path match the current texture handle and generation. As a minimum safe correction, require `!texture->is_png` for the indexed-stock comparison and log `compare=0` with a replacement-specific reason; retain GPU hashes and samples without claiming a mismatch.
- Validation: In paired D1 and D2 Android runs, load stock, same-size PNG, different-size PNG, same-size KTX2, and different-size KTX2 fixtures with deliberately distinct corner, center, palette, alpha, and super-transparency pixels. Require stock expected comparisons and exact zero mismatches, replacement comparisons against their own uploaded source when retained or an explicit unavailable status otherwise, no stock expected hash for replacements, and correct behavior after cache smash, palette reload, replacement enable/disable, and GL-handle reuse.
- Resolution: Pending

- Evidence: Both paired renderers call `android_merged_wall_track_face` for every valid cached or two-pass face with a secondary texture. The defect is most likely in complex or custom levels where the diagnostic is needed to explain a crowded rendering failure, and equivalent geometry can produce different results when render order changes.

- Suggested fix: Track a complete dynamically sized per-frame candidate list within engine draw bounds, then retain only the best output records after named-target, polygon-hit, distance, visibility, and draw-order ranking. If fixed storage is required, maintain a seen count and overflow state and replace the current worst candidate using the same deterministic ranking policy already used by the 64-entry draw-face probe. Place the only named or crosshair face first, at index 31, 32, and last and reverse submission order. Require identical selected identity and cover evidence for every ordering, an exact seen/omitted count if bounded, no dangling cover-event indices during replacement, and an explicit non-success status whenever complete ranking cannot be guaranteed.

The comparator then considers only that bucket, bounding-box distance, overlap area, cover order, draw order, and event index. Exact polygon hits therefore appear only in logs and do not improve rank, although the separate crosshair-target admission predicate explicitly accepts them. For a skewed quad or triangle, the crosshair can lie inside its AABB but outside its polygon; that false-positive candidate receives the same or better center bucket as a true polygon hit and can win on overlap area or later draw order. Diagnostic comparisons can consequently attribute a rendering defect to the wrong texture or draw path while reporting a center-focused result.
- Expected: When valid projected polygons are available, an exact face or cover polygon hit outranks any candidate supported only by bounding-box containment; bounding boxes remain a fallback for incomplete projection, with deterministic tie-breaking among equivalent exact hits.
- Suggested fix: Add screen- and canvas-space polygon-hit tiers ahead of bounding-box tiers in the focus bucket or comparator, and define whether face, cover, or their true polygonal intersection has precedence. After resolving BR-0308's coordinate contract, calculate and rank one canonical crosshair space rather than mixing screen and canvas variants. Publish the winning hit kind so consumers can distinguish exact geometry from fallback.
- Validation: Add paired D1 and D2 focus-cover fixtures with convex quads, skewed/rotated quads, and triangles whose AABBs overlap the crosshair. Pair a box-only false positive with a true polygon hit, reverse draw and cover order, and vary overlap area; require the true hit to win in full-screen and offset cockpit/subcanvas modes. Also cover incomplete projections to verify the documented bounding-box fallback and ties between multiple true hits.

- Evidence: Only `HIT_WALL` supplies an intersected segment, side, and point. The function then creates a valid draw context and returns `1`, despite never testing the chosen side against the ray or crosshair. Its caller reduces that success to `geometry_hit`, publishes `hit_kind=POLYGON`, and sets both `center_polygon_hit` and `center_bbox_hit` to one. - Impact: The probe can report an arbitrary segment side and its base/overlay textures as the polygon under the crosshair, then emit palette, GL texture, wall, door, UV, and readback evidence for that unrelated side. Automated or manual rendering investigations can accept a complete-looking `geometry_hit` and diagnose the wrong asset or route precisely when the actual ray query failed.
- Expected: A geometry hit is published only after FVI returns `HIT_WALL` with a valid intersected segment and side. `HIT_NONE`, `HIT_BAD_P0`, and invalid hit metadata remain explicit non-hit or indeterminate outcomes and never set polygon or bbox containment fields.
- Suggested fix: Return failure for every non-`HIT_WALL` FVI result and preserve the exact fate/status in the probe result. If the nearest side remains useful as secondary context, publish it in separate fallback fields with `hit_kind=NONE`, `center_polygon_hit=0`, and an explicit `forced_candidate` status; do not feed it through `find_hitpoint_uv` or hit-dependent texture attribution without an actual intersection.

For non-hit cases, require the exact fate and start-segment diagnostics, no fabricated segment-side texture attribution, and stable fallback behavior when rendered-face candidates are present or absent.

### BR-0319: P2 - Advance the synthesizer while seeking through elapsed MIDI time

- Category: correctness/audio

- Related: `android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/midi_preview.c:L287-L340,L571-L585`, `android/app/src/main/java/com/dxxredux/app/MidiBytesPreviewDialog.kt:L63-L75,L155-L168`, TinySoundFont `tsf.h` envelope progression and `tsf_channel_note_off`, and archived BR-0028
- Evidence: Seek resets TinySoundFont, rewinds the message list, and calls note, controller, program, and pitch APIs for every event through the target, but it never renders or otherwise advances the synthesizer for the elapsed time between those events. TinySoundFont advances attack, hold, decay, sustain, release, sample position, modulation, and voice retirement only while rendering samples. A note that began seconds before the target is therefore recreated at its initial envelope and sample position instead of its target state; a note-on and note-off both before the target can enter release without any intervening attack or decay, and completed release voices are not retired according to elapsed time. The implementation comment claims MIDI seek requires re-rendering from the start, while the actual fast-forward explicitly processes events without rendering. Serialization under archived BR-0028 removes the race but does not correct this state reconstruction.
- Trigger: While a MIDI or HMP preview is playing or paused, seek past notes with nonzero attack, hold, decay, release, sample offset, modulation, or sustain history, especially deep into a dense track
- Impact: Audio after the seek can restart old samples, use the wrong envelope phase, retain stale release voices, omit notes that should still sustain, or steal voices from the actual target passage. The same target sounds different from uninterrupted playback, so the launcher preview cannot reliably audition a selected position.
- Expected: Completing a seek produces synthesizer, channel, voice, sample, and envelope state equivalent to rendering the same file linearly through the target, apart from explicitly documented bounded resampling tolerance.
- Suggested fix: Replay events in timestamp order while rendering each elapsed interval into a bounded discard buffer, including the partial interval through the exact target, then clear only the output ring before resuming audible production. If deep seeks need acceleration, introduce validated synthesizer checkpoints containing all time-dependent state rather than skipping sample advancement.
- Validation: Create MIDI fixtures with isolated long attack, sustained note, early note-off with long release, pitch and controller changes, repeated same-key voices, percussion, and voice counts above and below the configured limit. Capture a short PCM window after linear playback reaches each target and after direct seek to it at 44.1 and 48 kHz; require identical or tightly bounded samples, active voices, channel state, and position. Repeat while playing and paused and retain BR-0028's rapid concurrent-seek coverage.
- Additional location (R1-CHUNK-0203): `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/midi_preview.h:L47-L53` in the public seek contract
- Additional evidence (R1-CHUNK-0203): The header explicitly tells callers that MIDI seek requires and performs re-rendering from the start. The frozen implementation instead labels its loop as processing events without rendering audio and invokes no synth render function before publishing the target time. The public contract therefore confirms that linear-equivalent time advancement is intended rather than an accepted event-only approximation.
- Additional validation (R1-CHUNK-0203): Retain the public re-rendering claim only when the linear-versus-seek PCM and synth-state matrix passes; otherwise document a deliberately weaker approximation and expose that limitation to the launcher instead of promising equivalent reconstruction.

- Related: `android/app/src/main/cpp/CMakeLists.txt:L388-L397`, `d1/arch/ogl/ogl.c:L2792-L2808,L3317-L3345`, `d2/arch/ogl/ogl.c:L2802-L2818,L3400-L3444`, `android/app/src/main/java/com/dxxredux/app/ModManager.kt:L310-L375`, `android/app/src/main/java/com/dxxredux/app/DxaTextureScanner.kt:L52-L99`, and archived BR-0018
- Evidence: `read_png` limits only compressed input bytes to 256 MiB, then calls `stbi_load_from_memory` and materializes the complete decoded image before publishing its dimensions. Only afterward does the paired uploader round those dimensions and reject values above `ogl_max_texture_size`, capped at 2,048 on Android. The pinned stb_image v2.30 contract states that format limits generally permit decoded allocations just under one or two gigabytes and explicitly offers `STBI_MAX_DIMENSIONS` to prevent denial of service from gigantic untrusted images; this translation unit leaves the default 16,777,216-pixel dimension limit in place and performs no checked pixel-budget preflight. Direct DXA import enables arbitrary nonempty input. The launcher scanner merely displays that oversized PNG, TGA, or KTX2 entries “will be skipped,” does not block them, and does not inspect supported JPEG dimensions, so it neither protects nor accurately models the earlier native decode.

- Impact: Texture caching can allocate and touch hundreds of megabytes to nearly two gigabytes for data that the uploader immediately discards. On supported Android devices this can stall the game, trigger allocator or low-memory termination, or crash the process; the mod remains enabled, so loading the same texture can repeat the denial of service.
- Expected: Replacement dimensions, channel count, and checked decoded byte size are validated against the engine and process budgets before any full pixel allocation or decompression work.
- Suggested fix: Use `stbi_info_from_memory` on the bounded source buffer, reject nonpositive or over-cap dimensions and checked `width * height * output_channels` totals before `stbi_load_from_memory`, and define a conservative `STBI_MAX_DIMENSIONS` as defense in depth. Share the native limit with DXA scanning, inspect JPEG as well as every other admitted format, and prevent over-budget mods from being enabled instead of presenting a warning that decoding has already made unsafe.
- Validation: Exercise PNG, JPEG, and TGA fixtures with one through four channels, high compression ratios, dimensions and decoded totals immediately below and above each limit, extreme aspect ratios, multiplication boundaries, corrupt headers, masks, and ordinary 2,048-pixel replacements. Measure peak native heap and decode time in paired D1 and D2; require over-budget inputs to fail before pixel allocation, preserve stock fallback, and never terminate or materially stall the game.

- Suggested fix: Validate every packed size and image offset, upload levels `0..mip_count-1` with checked ETC2 dimensions, set `GL_TEXTURE_MAX_LEVEL` to `mip_count - 1`, and mark the texture's mip state only after the complete chain succeeds. On partial failure, delete the handle and fall back atomically; if authored mips are intentionally unsupported, stop copying them and generate a complete chain from level zero without retaining the zero-level clamp.
- Validation: Build mip-colored RGB and RGBA KTX2 fixtures with one level and complete and truncated multi-level chains, including non-square and padded original dimensions. - Suggested fix: Rank immediately usable sources as today, then transactionally attempt each remaining source in a deterministic cost order. Restore the complete dependency state after each failed attempt, retain the strongest failure only if all candidates fail, and avoid a trigger without excluding distinct triggers that open the same side. Keep source-local in-progress markers so genuine cycles still terminate.

### BR-0334: P2 - Measure portal clearance instead of destination-center clearance

- [ ] OPEN

- Location: `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/secret_area_game_adapter.c:L1453-L1500` in topology clearance construction

- Evidence: The adapter computes one binary clearance value per destination segment by placing a player-sized sphere only at that segment's cached center. If the center does not intersect a wall it returns the full player radius; otherwise it returns one. The continuation then copies that destination scalar to every incoming side, without inspecting the side vertices, portal aperture, source geometry, or a swept path through the connection. Route search treats any copied value at least as large as the navigator radius as proof that the side is traversable. A roomy destination behind a portal narrower than the player therefore passes solely because its center is clear. The inverse heuristic is also topology-dependent: the code acknowledges that skewed but navigable segments can have bad centers, yet relaxes only connected bad-center components smaller than three; three or more such segments retain clearance one and are rejected without testing an off-center route. Snapshot tests inject a clearance number directly and never exercise the engine adapter's derivation.

The inverse geometry is reported partial or failed even though the player can traverse it, and the arbitrary component-size threshold makes equivalent local geometry change solvability when a third segment is attached.
- Expected: Navigator clearance describes the actual directed connection and a realizable player-sized traversal through its portal; destination-center occupancy alone neither proves nor disproves passage clearance.
- Suggested fix: Compute clearance per side from the portal polygon and adjacent segment geometry, then validate a player-radius swept transition or bounded set of connected occupiable poses across the side. Preserve an explicit unknown state that route search handles conservatively rather than treating zero as unrestricted, and remove the component-count relaxation once valid off-center traversal is represented.
- Validation: Add paired adapter-level geometry fixtures for wide and too-narrow portals between roomy segments, asymmetric portal directions, a clear center with blocked transition, one through four skewed but navigable segments with off-center paths, and genuinely narrow tunnels. It scans canonical steps with narrow completion predicates, validates a firing position only when the selected step is a shoot switch, then copies the complete canonical state and summary without comparing any current fingerprint, start segment, object position, navigation state, or downstream reachability. It does not perform the cache plan's required short pathfinding; instead it fabricates a one-segment pending path terminating at the canonical step's authored segment. A concrete shipped caller exposes the stale-object case: local and replicated D2 boss teleports relink the boss, clear an active boss goal, and mark metadata dirty specifically to replan. Refresh captures the boss's new segment and object hash, but reuse ignores them and restores the canonical boss step. - Impact: Guide-Bot can immediately resume guiding toward the boss's pre-teleport segment and remain detached from the live objective. More generally, a refresh can advertise an `ok` reused route and downstream waypoints that are no longer reachable in the current snapshot, defeating the event invalidation and exposing stale route state through introspection and automation.
- Expected: A live refresh rebases semantic steps onto the current start and snapshot, recomputes a real short path to the first pending objective, and falls back to full planning whenever current object, navigation, trigger, progression, or path state cannot prove compatibility.
- Suggested fix: Move live reuse into an explicit planner rebase operation that consumes the canonical semantic sequence plus the current snapshot and query. Match pending object objectives to current live objects, validate all skipped-step effects and retained downstream assumptions, run bounded pathfinding from the current start to the selected objective, and return false on any mismatch so the existing full-planner fallback runs. Do not synthesize a path count or terminal segment.
- Validation: Add paired snapshot tests that mutate start segment, boss segment and position, key carrier, wall lock or opening state, trigger effects, and downstream reachability after canonical planning. Require either a newly pathfound compatible reuse or a full fallback, never a stale canonical terminal. ### BR-0336: P2 - Close route-cache files after short reads

- [ ] OPEN
- Type: defect
- Confidence: high
- Category: resource-lifetime
- Found by: R1-CHUNK-0216
- Location: `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/secret_area_game_adapter.c:L1881-L1929` in persistent route-cache loading
- Related: `android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/route_analysis_cache.c:L117-L252`, `android/tests/test_route_analysis_cache.c`, and `android/ai tool plans/gameplay/route_cache_android_audit_20260715.md`
- Evidence: After accepting the reported exact record length and allocating a buffer, the loader combines the complete-read check, `PHYSFS_close(file)`, and decode with `&&`. C evaluates those operands left to right with short-circuiting. If `PHYSFS_readBytes` returns fewer bytes or an error, the close operand is never evaluated. The buffer is freed and the cache is rejected, but the open PhysicsFS file and its underlying descriptor remain owned indefinitely; this branch also increments only `rejections`, not `io_errors`. The length-mismatch and allocation-failure branches close explicitly, so the leak is isolated to a read that becomes short after the length check.
- Trigger: Make an app-private route-cache record report the exact expected length, then truncate or replace it between `PHYSFS_fileLength` and `PHYSFS_readBytes`, inject a filesystem read error, or otherwise return a short read; repeat level loads while the failing record remains addressable.
- Impact: Each failed cache attempt leaks a PhysicsFS handle and native file descriptor until process exit. Repeated mission or level loads under a persistent storage failure or cache mutation can exhaust descriptors and cause unrelated asset, save, music, or cache opens to fail.
- Expected: Every successful `PHYSFS_openRead` is closed exactly once on every read, decode, allocation, and validation outcome, and read failures are counted as I/O errors before falling back to planning.
- Suggested fix: Store the read result, call `PHYSFS_close` unconditionally in a separate statement, and only then combine read, close, and decode results. Classify short or failed reads and close failures as I/O errors while retaining rejection and safe planner fallback behavior.
- Validation: Add an injectable PhysicsFS loader test that reports the exact record length but returns a short read or error, plus a close-failure case. Assert one close per successful open, no increase in process descriptor count over repeated attempts, no decode on incomplete bytes, correct I/O and rejection counters, and successful full-planner fallback.
- Resolution: Pending

- Related: `android/app/src/main/cpp/shared/android_save_set.c:L48-L85`, `android/tests/test_android_save_set.c:L29-L58`, `d1/main/mission.c:L251-L303`, `d2/main/mission.c:L352-L420`, `d1/main/state.c:L1787-L1797`, `d2/main/state.c:L1880-L1890`, and BR-0207
- Evidence: Both mission loaders retain the complete descriptor basename without a 15-byte limit, and the save-set path builder is designed to sanitize as many as 31 bytes into `mission_dir`. The shared state layer nevertheless declares `char mission[16]` and copies `Current_mission_filename` into it before every ordinary single-player core save. Regular load similarly reads the full mission written to `last_single.txt` back through that same 16-byte destination. Therefore distinct accepted missions whose basenames share the first 15 bytes resolve every core slot to the identical pilot/mission pathname. Saving slot N in the second mission truncates and replaces slot N from the first mission; autosave progress, exit, minimize, and periodic slots collide the same way. The file's Android metadata still records the complete second mission name, while D2 secret companions use the save-set builder's wider 31-byte mission component, so one visible save generation can combine a shared overwritten core namespace with mission-distinct sidecar namespaces. The focused path test checks only short `d2` and `descent` names and never passes through the narrowing shared-state wrapper. BR-0207 covers a separate 31-byte rewind-history truncation symptom; it establishes the same unbounded accepted mission identity but does not cover durable save-slot collisions.
- Trigger: Import and play two supported D1 or D2 custom missions with descriptor basenames such as `abcdefghijklmnop_a` and `abcdefghijklmnop_b`, use the same pilot, and save or autosave the same slot in each
- Impact: The later mission silently overwrites the earlier mission's manual or lifecycle save without any collision warning or separate slot identity. The load menu, Save Explorer metadata, and D2 secret companion can then describe different mission generations, and the player loses the prior mission's only saved progress despite the feature promising mission-masked save sets.
- Expected: Every mission identity accepted by the engine maps deterministically to its own collision-resistant save-set namespace, and core saves, last-save pointers, metadata, and D2 companions use the same canonical identity.
- Suggested fix: Define one shared mission-identity encoder used by all save-set artifacts. Preserve the complete canonical basename when practical or combine a readable bounded prefix with a collision-resistant digest; never narrow it before the canonical encoder. Version the last-save pointer and migrate legacy 15-byte directories without overwriting an already distinct set.
- Validation: Add paired D1 and D2 integration tests with basenames of 15, 16, 31, 32, and near-`PATH_MAX` bytes, two names sharing the first 15 and two sharing the first 31, separator and case-normalization variants, and existing legacy directories. Save distinct hashes to every manual and autosave slot, restart, load through the ordinary menu and Save Explorer, and assert every mission recovers only its own core, metadata, pointer, and D2 companion with no overwrite or ambiguous migration.

### BR-0339: P1 - Clamp the network overlay within narrow displays

- [ ] OPEN
- Type: defect
- Confidence: high
- Category: correctness
- Found by: R1-CHUNK-0219
- Location: `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:android/app/src/main/java/com/dxxredux/app/multiplayer/NetworkEventsOverlay.kt:L84-L97,L216-L228` in draw-time sizing
- Related: `android/app/src/main/java/com/dxxredux/app/MainActivity.kt:L728-L731,L794-L801,L2230-L2248`, `android/app/src/main/java/com/dxxredux/app/SetupActivity.kt:L4765-L4800`, and `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:L51-L57`
- Evidence: Panel width is computed with `(w * 0.32f).coerceIn(160f * density, w * 0.45f)`. Kotlin requires the minimum not exceed the maximum; for every view narrower than `160 / 0.45 = 355.56dp`, this call receives an empty range and throws `IllegalArgumentException` from `onDraw`. The application declares no minimum screen width, exposes and applies a portrait game orientation, and supports configuration changes without recreating the activity. The outer activity automatically calls `show` while a multiplayer launch has not yet reached in-game state and while the host is selecting players, so the crash does not require an obscure direct call or even a manual diagnostic toggle. No test constructs the view or measures it at narrow widths.
- Trigger: Select portrait orientation on a device whose available game width is below 356dp, or place the game in a comparably narrow supported multi-window, then start or host a multiplayer game so the network-events overlay is automatically shown
- Impact: The game process crashes on its first network-overlay draw, preventing multiplayer startup or host player selection on the affected display configuration
- Expected: Diagnostic overlay measurement is total for every nonnegative view size Android can deliver, fits within the available viewport and insets, and never throws because a preferred minimum exceeds the current maximum
- Suggested fix: Derive one nonnegative available content width after padding and insets, choose the preferred width, then clamp it with an ordering-safe `min` against that available width rather than passing a potentially inverted interval to `coerceIn`. Skip drawing at zero size and truncate, wrap, or scroll rows within the bounded rectangle.
- Validation: Add a view or screenshot test across zero width and 240, 320, 355, 356, 360, 600, and large-screen dp widths at several densities, portrait and landscape, cutouts, and multi-window resizing while the overlay is hidden, manually visible, and automatically visible during multiplayer phases. Require no exception and assert the background and every rendered row remain inside the viewport.

### BR-0340: P2 - Stop network overlay polling when its view detaches

- [ ] OPEN
- Type: defect
- Confidence: high
- Category: resource-lifetime
- Found by: R1-CHUNK-0219
- Location: `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:android/app/src/main/java/com/dxxredux/app/multiplayer/NetworkEventsOverlay.kt:L23-L60` in self-reposting main-looper polling
- Related: `android/app/src/main/java/com/dxxredux/app/MainActivity.kt:L1771-L1784,L2081-L2292,L2419-L2441`
- Evidence: Once `show` sets `polling`, the runnable captures its overlay, invokes the provider, invalidates, and reposts itself every second. Only explicit `hide` clears the flag and removes that callback; the view has no detach hook. `MainActivity.onStop` removes callbacks from a different `overlayPoller` but does not hide this overlay, and `onDestroy` neither hides it nor clears its provider. If the network overlay is visible when the activity backgrounds or is destroyed, its queued runnable therefore continues forever on the process main looper. The runnable retains the view, whose `Context` retains the destroyed `MainActivity` and its game view graph; repeated sessions can accumulate one retained activity and periodic callback each.
- Trigger: Show the network-events overlay manually or reach an automatically visible multiplayer phase, then background the game, return to the launcher, finish the activity, or recreate it without first executing an explicit overlay-hide branch
- Impact: Background work continues once per second, and destroyed game activities and their large view graphs remain reachable. Repeated game launches can accumulate memory and main-looper work until process death or memory pressure, while detached views receive pointless invalidations.
- Expected: Polling is active only while the view is attached, visible, and owned by a live resumed activity, and every lifecycle exit removes all callbacks and provider references deterministically
- Suggested fix: Start polling from an attached-and-visible lifecycle and unconditionally stop it in `onDetachedFromWindow`; also have `MainActivity.onStop` or `onDestroy` hide or dispose every polling overlay. Clear `stateProvider` on disposal, and use one lifecycle-aware scheduler rather than independent self-reposting handlers where practical.
- Validation: Add lifecycle tests that show the overlay, stop, detach, destroy, recreate, and repeat without an explicit manual hide. Advance the main looper past several intervals and assert no provider calls or callbacks remain, the old activity is garbage-collectable, and resuming or reattaching starts exactly one polling chain.

- Evidence: The assigned panel intentionally remains present while `DISCONNECTED` whenever any STUN address, candidate map, connectivity pair, connection record, or relay assignment remains, and it renders those values without a connection or lobby generation. If historical diagnostics are desired, store them separately with terminal status and timestamps.

### BR-0342: P1 - Authenticate LAN lobby control packets and member identities

- [ ] OPEN
- Type: defect
- Confidence: high
- Category: security/protocol-integrity
- Found by: R1-CHUNK-0220
- Location: `c01d8fe4686c63d931b1e543a6305bbafaa944a9:android/app/src/main/java/com/dxxredux/app/lobby/LobbyProtocol.kt:L14-L26,L110-L260,L298-L328` in the unauthenticated JSON-over-UDP lobby message schema and parser
- Related: `android/app/src/main/java/com/dxxredux/app/lobby/LobbyService.kt:L630-L683,L870-L968,L1099-L1155,L1221-L1260`, `android/app/src/main/java/com/dxxredux/app/multiplayer/NetworkConstants.kt:L40-L50`, `android/app/src/main/java/com/dxxredux/app/SetupActivity.kt:L1701-L1740`, and `android/app/src/test/java/com/dxxredux/app/LobbyProtocolStartOptionsTest.kt:L15-L58`
- Evidence: Every LAN lobby datagram is plaintext JSON with a message type and payload fields but no authenticated session, host credential, member credential, sequence, or replay generation. The lobby UUID is broadcast in `ANNOUNCE`, so matching it proves no authority. On the frozen host, `LEAVE` and `READY` select another player solely by payload callsign, and `CHAT` accepts and relays any payload callsign from any sender without requiring membership. On a joiner, `PLAYER_LIST`, `JOIN_REJECT`, and `KICK` do not receive the sender address at all; `JOIN_ACK` accepts any nonempty lobby ID and binds its sender as host without correlating a pending target; and `START` checks at most the public lobby ID, not that the sender is the joined host. The accepted `START` payload becomes a launch event using that sender as `lanHostAddr` and trusts its port, game, mission, mode, difficulty, level, maximum-player count, and options; unsupported modes then silently map to anarchy. The focused test proves ordinary serialization only and has no hostile-sender, identity, replay, or state-transition cases. Later sender/client-ID checks added for `LEAVE` and `READY` do not authenticate the remaining host-control and chat messages.
- Trigger: While another player hosts or joins a discoverable lobby, let any device able to send UDP on the same LAN observe the broadcast lobby ID and transmit forged `LEAVE`, `READY`, `CHAT`, `PLAYER_LIST`, `JOIN_ACK`, `JOIN_REJECT`, `KICK`, or `START` JSON datagrams to port 42400
- Impact: A malicious or compromised LAN peer can impersonate players, change readiness, remove members, falsify the roster, abort or redirect a join, eject joined clients, and force a client to leave setup and launch the native game toward an attacker-selected address and port with attacker-selected mission and rules. Replayed stale control packets can also affect a later state that reuses the same process and lobby identity.
- Expected: Only the established host can alter joiner state or launch and kick a client, only an admitted member can act or chat as that identity, every response is correlated with the exact pending lobby generation, and stale, forged, cross-lobby, or semantically invalid packets are rejected without changing UI or launch state
- Suggested fix: Establish a high-entropy per-lobby host identity and a distinct per-member session credential during a correlated join handshake, then authenticate every state-changing datagram with an AEAD or MAC over its type, lobby/generation ID, sender role, member ID, sequence number, and payload. Bind acknowledgements and rejections to the requested host and nonce, enforce monotonic replay windows, verify exact source and role as an additional check, validate all launch enums and numeric ranges before publication, and rotate credentials whenever hosting or membership restarts.
- Validation: Add a two-client hostile-peer matrix for every message type covering wrong source, wrong member, copied callsign, public lobby ID, unsolicited and mismatched acknowledgements, spoofed rejection and player list, kick for another target, forged and replayed start, reordered and duplicate sequence numbers, stale packets after leave/rejoin and host restart, and malformed launch fields. Assert no unauthorized state, liveness timestamp, chat attribution, retry cancellation, membership, readiness, diagnostic, or launch event changes; then verify ordinary join, reconnect, mid-game join, chat, ready, kick, start, packet loss, and app resume still work.
- Resolution: Pending
